summary: My SHOULD-FIX is repaired in the strongest of the three forms I offered: venue and pin are now the same object, the 2018 Mac mini is abandoned, and the 2025 last-x86_64-image recital is withdrawn. The mechanics remain clean — I simulated all five edits and the register comes out at eighteen named identifiers, one reserved cell which is G13, and zero survivals of PARTLY MET. But in making the venue the pin, the entry re-pinned all four platforms, and three of them now differ in memory from D-006's named class while the entry asserts the thresholds are unchanged. D-006 says in terms that all ms and RSS numbers bind to that class, so re-binding them to different machines changes what they require, in opposite directions on different platforms, and the entry records neither the analysis nor a warrant that reaches beyond Intel scarcity.

objections.location: Subject, 'Scoped D-006 successor (runner class only)' and 'Exact pins', read against D-006's reference-runner-class clause and against this entry's own 'Thresholds unchanged'
objections.claim: The successor re-pins all four platform classes, three at memory sizes different from D-006's, while asserting D-006's numbers are unchanged. D-006 binds those numbers to the class, so the re-binding silently changes what they require — and it changes it in opposite directions across platforms.
objections.why: D-006's clause is explicit: 'all ms/RSS numbers bind to this runner class — macOS arm64: base-configuration Apple Silicon entry chip (M1-class), 8 GB; macOS x86_64: native Intel-class hardware, never Rosetta-on-Apple-Silicon; Linux x86_64 and arm64: 4-vCPU / 8 GB standard cloud-runner class.' Against that, the new pins read: macos-arm64-ref as a 3-core Apple M1 with 7 GB, which is fewer cores and less memory than a base-configuration M1 machine; linux-x86_64-ref and linux-arm64-ref as 4 CPU with 16 GB, which is double the memory D-006 named at the same vCPU count. Only macos-x86_64-ref lacked a size in D-006 and so cannot conflict. The consequence is not neutral and is not in one direction. On macOS arm64 the same cold-start milliseconds must now be met on a smaller machine, which makes the gate stricter; on both Linux platforms they must be met on a machine with twice the memory, which makes it laxer. The entry says 'Thresholds unchanged', 'Numeric thresholds stand', and rejects an alternative to 'Change D-006 numeric thresholds' as out of scope. All of that is true of the numerals and none of it is true of what the numerals assert, because D-006 attached them to a class this entry replaces. D-006 also sets the standard for how such a move is recorded: its falsifiability note requires that when a number proves infeasible 'the lawful path is a successor decision with the measurement attached — never a silent waiver'. Here the class moves rather than the number, no measurement accompanies it, and the effect on the bar is unstated. There is a second, related gap in the warrant. The entry says 'This entry is the OBS-T3-02 successor-decision path for the runner class only', and OBS-T3-02 reads 'native Intel Mac hardware is scarcity-exposed … unprocurability routes through this entry's successor-decision path'. That route plainly supports re-pinning the Intel machine. It does not on its face reach macOS arm64 or the two Linux classes, none of which had a procurability problem. The entry may well hold authority for a broader PREFERENCE-LADEN successor under D-000, but it rests a four-platform re-pin on an observation about Intel scarcity without saying so.
objections.whyNotMustFix: The facts are disclosed rather than hidden — each pin states its exact CPU and RAM, so a reader can see the 7 GB and the 16 GB. Nothing false is written into file 08 either: the inserted cells say 'D-006 runner-class successor + exact GH-hosted pins', which is accurate, and no numeric threshold is altered anywhere. The naming act itself is sound on the new pins, so condition 4's arithmetic does not depend on this objection. What is missing is the analysis and the stated warrant, not the underlying disclosure.
objections.repair: Record the trade in bytes, as D-002 and D-006 both do for their own preference-laden choices: state per platform how the new venue compares with D-006's named class, and whether the existing ms and RSS numbers remain the intended bar on it, under the same product sign-off. Where a platform's venue is now larger, say that the bar is thereby easier and that this is accepted, or re-derive the number. And either widen the stated warrant beyond OBS-T3-02 to the D-000 preference-laden authority actually being used, or confine the successor to the Intel class that OBS-T3-02 names.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The repair to my turn-1 finding is the right one and the most honest of the three routes I offered: rather than defend the mini pin, the entry abandons it, says plainly that it was never verified procurable, withdraws the recital that supported it, and makes the venue and the pin one object. That is a better outcome than the alternative I would have accepted. The new objection is a consequence of that repair rather than a repeat of the old one. Making the venue the pin meant re-pinning every platform, and three of the four now sit at memory sizes D-006 did not name — 7 GB where it said 8, and 16 GB where it said 8, twice. D-006's own sentence is that all ms and RSS numbers bind to the class, so those numbers now ask for the same milliseconds on a smaller Mac and on Linux machines with double the memory. The entry says thresholds are unchanged, and the numerals are; what they demand is not. This corpus records that kind of trade in bytes rather than leaving it to be inferred, and the warrant cited — an observation about Intel scarcity — does not by itself reach the three platforms that had no scarcity problem.
